n2.text: Under 1000px the panels are drawers. Under 640px the zoom readout and Fit hide so the toolbar stays on one row.

n3.text:
Easel drawn in Easel. Edit these boards to redesign the app.
assets/easel.css holds the chrome styles; app/src/style.css mirrors it.

n4.text: Shipped 2026-11-10 (first run, AI readiness and failure, comment write lock), shown on these boards

p0s.text:
Nothing below is built yet. Each row is one decision; where a row has A / B / C, one of them is picked.
Recommended: Share → A first, B as a switch on A, C later. Activity → B on the board, with the history menu from C as the log.

p1.text: 1 · Share a view-only copy  (pick A, B or C)

p1a.text:
A · Export folder — recommended first
1. One Share button in the toolbar. Ask AI stays the only filled action.
2. Scope comes first: whole canvas, this page, or the selected boards.
3. Web folder is the main row: static files for Vercel, GitHub Pages or a PR preview. PDF and PNG sit below.
4. The result stays in the popover: path, Reveal, Copy deploy command.
5. Same thing from the terminal: npx easel-canvas export.
Trade-off: it needs a place to host. In return it runs in CI and gives Easel a public demo.

p1b.text:
What the viewer opens (same page for A, B and C)
1. No editing tools: canvas name, pages, zoom, Play.
2. A stamp says what this is: view only, export time, commit.
3. Comments and notes come along, read-only.
4. Play is the one filled button, a reviewer's first click.
5. "Made with Easel" in the corner.

p1c.text:
B · Single file
1. Same popover; the first row is one .html file with everything inside.
2. No hosting: attach it to Slack, email or a PR.
3. The size is shown before saving.
Trade-off: large canvases make large files, and nothing updates after sending. Better as a --single-file switch on A than as its own feature.

p1d.text:
C · Live link (also covers "view together")
1. A switch, not an export: on while Easel runs.
2. The link, then Can view / Can comment.
3. Who is looking now and where: cursors and selection on the canvas.
4. Comments from the link are marked "via link". Files change only on this computer.
Trade-off: needs a tunnel and this computer left on. Most work and most risk, so later.

p2.text: 2 · Who changed what  (pick A, B or C)

p2a.text:
A · Activity tab
1. A third tab in the right panel, filtered by Everyone / AI / People.
2. Each entry: who (agent colour), what, where, when.
3. Open an entry: before and after of the element, the request behind it, Compare, Undo.
4. One AI run is one group that folds.
Trade-off: complete, but out of sight until the tab is opened.

p2b.text:
B · On the board — recommended
1. A tag above the changed board: who · when · how many changes.
2. The changed element is outlined in that agent's colour.
3. Click the tag: the change, Before / After, Undo.
4. Tags fade once seen and clear after a day.
Trade-off: no full log by itself. Pair it with the history menu from C.

p2c.text:
C · Toast + history menu
1. A toast when someone else changes a file: who, what, Compare, Undo.
2. Undo gets a ▾: the history list with names, and "Go back to here".
3. Nothing new in the panels.
Trade-off: lightest, and easy to miss after time away. Recommended as the log half of B.

p3a.text:
Permission requests and formatted answers
1. When the agent asks to run something, the chat shows a card with the exact command: Allow once / Always allow / Deny.
2. The run waits, and the status says "Waiting for you".
3. Earlier decisions fold into one line, in time order.
4. Answers render markdown: lists, code, bold.

p3b.text:
Undo a whole AI run
1. Each run ends with a result row: boards changed and added, as chips.
2. "Undo this run" takes back the whole run in one step. Compare shows before and after.
3. An undone run stays in the chat with Redo.
4. After a restart the undo list is gone, so the row offers "Restore the copy from before this run".

p3c.text:
More agents
1. The picker lists Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent and Gemini CLI with today's status words.
2. Not installed: one line and "How to install".
3. "Custom command…" for anything else: a name and a command with {prompt}.
4. "Check again" re-reads what is installed.

p4.text: 4 · Several people and agents on one canvas

p4a.text:
Who is on which board
1. A board being edited says who: "Claude Code is editing…", "You · editing".
2. A second agent sent to a busy board works on a fork next to it, with an arrow back to the original.
3. When both are done, either one takes "Use this one".
4. The same colour dot in the board list.

p4b.text:
Pick one of the variants
1. Every variant gets "Use this".
2. The confirm says what happens: the original is replaced, the others go to trash. "Keep all" is the other answer.
3. A toast with Undo afterwards.
4. Variants land in the first free row, never on top of notes or boards.

p4c.text:
Select and edit without entering Edit mode
1. Click an element on a board: a small toolbar with Text, Fill, Radius, Spacing, Ask AI, Comment.
2. Fill offers tokens first, then Custom.
3. A breadcrumb shows board › element.
4. The right panel uses design words (Fill, Corner radius, Padding, Gap); the CSS name shows on hover.
The largest change of the set.
